bodies.name: Cairn
bodies.class: cold, cloudy world with a dense atmosphere

lattice.where: Shallow seams under the stone fields

control.note: Claims pending the Bench's ruling on sapience

bodies.notes: Cold and cloudy, with a dense atmosphere and an overcast that almost never breaks. Colonial organisms build stone structures several meters high, some in rows and rings that run for kilometers, and the structures appear to respond to nearby lattice. Survey footage shows some standing hundreds of meters from where they were recorded a week earlier. A Bench xenobiologist has reported that the organisms meet the Charter's threshold for possible sapience.

bodies.gmNotes: Its moon Cairn IIIa may be habitable; nobody has looked.

bodies.notes: A moon of Cairn III warmed by tidal heating, with life around its vents. Nobody has looked.

bodies.notes: A cold karst world riddled with caves and crystal caverns. Southern League prospectors have filed on it.

bodies.notes: Bench inspectors watching Cairn from orbit since their team was turned back at the landing site.

bodies.name: Scald mouth
bodies.notes: Mouth of the 5-day lane to Scald.

bodies.name: Deeps mouth
bodies.notes: Mouth of the 11-day lane to the Deeps (one way, outward from here). At the edge of the region.

places.name: The stone fields
places.notes: Rows and rings of stone built by Cairn's colonial organisms, running for kilometers. The organisms gather where the lattice seams beneath are thickest, and nobody has yet mined here without disturbing the structures nearby.

places.name: Kerr-Varga mines
places.notes: Kerr-Varga is racing to get its mines working before the Bench rules on whether the organisms are sapient. A finding of sapience would void every claim on the planet.

places.name: Cairn landing site
places.notes: Where Kerr-Varga's works militia met the Bench's inspection team in 5029u and turned it back after nine days.

places.name: Southern League claims
places.notes: Claims filed by Southern League holders alongside Kerr-Varga's.

places.name: The Great Ring (WIP)
places.notes: The largest stone ring yet recorded, several kilometers across, which survey footage shows turning slowly over weeks.

places.name: Listener camp (WIP)
places.notes: Listeners living among the stone fields, convinced the structures are answering the lattice.
